questions.question: Which statement best captures the combined role of data sampling and dimensionality reduction in data reduction strategies?

options.A: Both techniques create a completely new dataset that discards the original information.
options.B: Both aim to produce a smaller representation of the data while preserving the analytical usefulness of the original set.
options.C: Sampling reduces attributes, whereas dimensionality reduction reduces the number of tuples.
options.D: Neither technique affects the size of the data; they only improve visualisation.

questions.explanation:
Both sampling (a form of numerosity reduction) and dimensionality reduction are described as ways to obtain a reduced representation of the data that is much smaller in volume yet yields the same (or almost the same) analytical results. [Page 4, Page 26]  

---

questions.question: What is the primary goal of dimensionality reduction as defined in the text?

options.A: To increase the number of random variables for richer analysis.
options.B: To replace data with alternative parametric models.
options.C: To reduce the number of random variables or attributes under consideration.
options.D: To compress data without any loss of information.

questions.explanation:
The text states that dimensionality reduction “is the process of reducing the number of random variables or attributes under consideration.” [Page 17]  

---

questions.question: In the context of numerosity reduction, which of the following methods is classified as non‑parametric?
questions.explanation:
Non‑parametric models listed for numerosity reduction include histograms, clusters, sampling, and data aggregation. Sampling is therefore a non‑parametric method. [Page 4]  

---

questions.question: Sampling allows a large dataset D containing N tuples to be represented by a much smaller random subset. Which implication follows from this description?

options.A: The subset will always contain exactly 10 % of the original tuples.
options.B: Analysis can be performed with reduced computational cost while still reflecting properties of the whole dataset.
options.C: The original dataset must be discarded after sampling.
options.D: Sampling guarantees identical analytical results to those obtained from the full dataset.

questions.explanation:
The text explains that sampling “allows a large data set to be represented by a much smaller random data sample (or subset),” implying reduced computational effort while preserving the dataset’s essential characteristics. [Page 26]  

---

questions.question: Why does the text emphasize that data reduction should produce “the same (or almost the same) analytical results”?

options.A: To ensure that the reduced data can be used for unrelated business processes.
options.B: To guarantee that the reduction process eliminates all noise from the data.
options.C: To make certain that conclusions drawn from the reduced data remain trustworthy and comparable to those from the original data.
options.D: To allow the reduced dataset to be stored in any file format.

questions.explanation:
Maintaining (almost) the same analytical results is essential so that the insights derived after reduction are still valid. [Page 4]  

---

questions.question: How does the text categorize dimensionality reduction and numerosity reduction with respect to data compression?

options.A: They are unrelated to data compression.
options.B: They are considered forms of data compression.
options.C: Only dimensionality reduction is a type of compression.
options.D: Only numerosity reduction can be lossless.

questions.explanation:
The passage notes that “Dimensionality reduction and numerosity reduction techniques can also be considered forms of data compression.” [Page 18]  

---

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between parametric and non‑parametric models used in numerosity reduction?

options.A: Parametric models require no assumptions about data distribution, while non‑parametric models do.
options.B: Parametric models assume a specific functional form (e.g., regression), whereas non‑parametric models do not (e.g., histograms, clustering).
options.C: Non‑parametric models always produce lossless compression, while parametric models are lossy.
options.D: Parametric models are only used for dimensionality reduction, not numerosity reduction.

questions.explanation:
The text lists regression and log‑linear models as parametric, and histograms, clusters, sampling, and aggregation as non‑parametric, reflecting the presence or absence of an assumed functional form. [Page 4]  

---

questions.question: Reducing the number of random variables through dimensionality reduction most directly yields which benefit mentioned in the context?

options.B: Simplified analysis and reduced computational complexity.
options.C: Complete elimination of all noise from the data.
options.D: Ability to apply any machine‑learning algorithm without modification.

questions.explanation:
By lowering the number of attributes, dimensionality reduction “reduces the number of random variables,” which naturally leads to simpler analysis and lower computational load. [Page 17]  

---

questions.question: The overview lists wavelet as one of the methods under dimensionality reduction. Which of the following best characterises why such methods are included in this category?

options.A: They increase the dimensionality of the data to improve visualization.
options.B: They transform data into a lower‑dimensional space while preserving important information.
options.C: They replace numeric attributes with textual descriptions.
options.D: They are used exclusively for lossless string compression.

questions.explanation:
Wavelet is cited as a dimensionality‑reduction method, implying it is used to transform data into fewer dimensions while retaining essential patterns. [Page 17]  

---

questions.question: Considering the data reduction strategies discussed, which combination would most effectively reduce data size while preserving analytical utility?

options.A: Applying only data compression algorithms without any sampling or dimensionality reduction.
options.B: Using dimensionality reduction to cut attributes and sampling to cut instances.
options.C: Performing numerosity reduction with only parametric models and no sampling.
options.D: Storing the full dataset in a three‑tier data‑warehouse architecture.

questions.explanation: The text highlights both dimensionality reduction (reducing attributes) and sampling (a form of numerosity reduction) as techniques that together achieve a much smaller dataset while maintaining analytical results. [Page 17, Page 26]
